samples.summary: New Markdown export writes document hrefs and image `src` into the downloaded file with no URL-scheme filter, unlike the PDF exporter which explicitly blocks `javascript:` / `data:`
samples.evidence: `exportMarkdownAndDownload` calls `serializeMarkdown(doc, { inlineImages: true })`. In `packages/docs/src/serialize/markdown.ts:216` a link is emitted as `[body](${escapeMarkdownHref(style.href)})` and at :239 an image as `![alt](${escapeMarkdownHref(image.src)})`; `escapeMarkdownHref` (:264) only backslash-escapes `)` and `\` — it performs no scheme check. `inlineImages: true` additionally disables the `[image]` placeholder that previously suppressed `data:` URIs (:235-238). The repo already treats exactly this as a threat on the sibling export sink: `packages/docs/src/export/pdf-painter.ts:831-834` filters `style.href` through `isSafeUrl` with the comment "so an imported document or paste-time mishap can't smuggle a `javascript:` / `data:` URI into a downloaded PDF". Attack: a collaborator (or a crafted .docx import) puts a run with `href = "javascript:..."` or an image with `src = "data:text/html;base64,..."` into a shared document; the victim exports Markdown; the produced `.md` carries the hostile URI verbatim and any renderer that resolves links (VS Code preview, a static site generator, a wiki paste) becomes the execution/exfiltration point. `isSafeUrl` is already exported from `@wafflebase/docs` (index.ts:185) and would have to be applied either in `serializeMarkdown` or by the new frontend wrapper.

samples.summary: New public mutating method `TextEditor.pasteFormat()` has no `this.readOnly` guard, unlike every sibling programmatic mutator; view-only enforcement now depends entirely on two call sites
samples.evidence: `pasteFormat()` (text-editor.ts:399-407) calls `this.saveSnapshot()` and `this.applyStyleToSelection(...)` — a document write — with no `if (this.readOnly) return;`. The class's other programmatic entry point does exactly that: `insertText()` at :674-677 ("View-only mode: block programmatic text injection"), as do the pointer/keyboard/composition handlers (:677, :730, :932, :1255, :1439). `TextEditor` is a public export of the package (packages/docs/src/index.ts:111) and is embedded by `TextBoxEditor` (view/text-box-editor.ts:48), which never passes `readOnly` at all. Today the only reachable paths are the keydown case (blocked by the read-only early-return at text-editor.ts:932-948) and `EditorAPI.pasteFormat`, which the hand-maintained allowlist neuters (editor.ts:3850), so I could not complete an exploit chain on this branch — but the class-level invariant "a mutating TextEditor method refuses in read-only" is now broken, and any future holder of a read-only TextEditor (e.g. a slides text-box mounted read-only, or a new EditorAPI passthrough) writes to a document the viewer may not own.

samples.summary: Read-only enforcement is a hand-maintained string allowlist plus a new ad-hoc special case, with nothing that fails when a mutating API member is forgotten
samples.evidence: `MUTATING_METHODS` (editor.ts:3830-3840) is a literal list of method names; this change correctly adds `setPageSetup`, but `pasteFormat` could not use the loop (it returns a boolean) and is patched separately at :3850. Nothing type-checks or tests that the union of the two covers every mutating `EditorAPI` member — the only coverage is per-method tests in `packages/docs/test/view/editor-read-only.test.ts`, each of which had to be written by hand (the diff adds two). A future mutating member added to `EditorAPI` (or a rename of one in the list — the array is `string`-typed, not `keyof EditorAPI`) silently ships an unneutered write path to viewers, while the surrounding comment makes the surface read as covered.

samples.summary: `safeFilename`, now extended to `.md`/`.txt`, strips only shell/FS metacharacters — not control characters, bidi overrides, or a leading dot — from an attacker-influenceable document title
samples.evidence: `safeFilename` replaces only `[\\/:*?"<>|]+` (export-utils.ts:110) and is fed straight into `a.download` (downloadBlob, :65). A document title is writable by any workspace member or share-link editor, so a title such as `report‮gpj.md` or `�invoice` or `.bashrc` yields a download name that renders with a spoofed extension or lands as a dotfile. Path traversal itself is blocked (`/` and `\` are replaced), so the impact is filename/extension spoofing on the victim's disk rather than an arbitrary write. Pre-existing helper, but this change widens its extension union and adds two new callers, so the sink now covers text formats users are more likely to open directly.
searchedFor: grep safeFilename call sites in packages/frontend/src/app/docs

samples.summary: A leaked agent tool-call fragment (`</content>` / `</invoke>`) is committed at the end of the new task doc
samples.evidence: Lines 79-80 of the new file are `</content>` followed by `</invoke>` — the tail of an unterminated tool invocation that was written into the repository as document content. It carries no instructions, so it is not an active prompt injection, but committing text that mimics tool-invocation framing into a file that future agents read is precisely the shape that lets a later, hostile edit in the same file be parsed as control flow rather than data. It should be deleted.

samples.summary: The format painter copies `href` (and `image`) along with visual formatting, so the new one-click toolbar button can silently propagate a hyperlink URL onto the painted selection
samples.evidence: `captureFormatAtCursor()` returns `{ ...raw, bold, italic, ... }` (text-editor.ts:3311-3319) — the spread of the caret run's raw `InlineStyle` carries `href` and `image` through unchanged, and `pasteFormat()` hands the whole buffer to `applyStyleToSelection`. Picking up a format while the caret sits inside a hyperlink therefore turns whatever the user next paints into a link to that URL. The behaviour is unchanged from the shortcut path, but `FormatPainterToggle` (docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:79-140) surfaces it as a discoverable one-click control labelled only "Copy formatting", so unintended link propagation — the kind a phishing-shaped href benefits from — becomes far more likely. Consider excluding `href`/`image` from the painter buffer.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. serializeMarkdown emits link targets and image sources verbatim: markdown.ts:216 `[body](escapeMarkdownHref(style.href))` and markdown.ts:239 `![alt](escapeMarkdownHref(image.src))`; escapeMarkdownHref (markdown.ts:264-266) only backslash-escapes `\` and `)` — no scheme allowlist. The full 267-line file imports nothing from view/url-detect.js or @wafflebase/core/url. The new frontend wrapper text-actions.ts:36-45 passes the document straight through with `inlineImages: true`, which additionally disables the `data:` -> `[image]` suppression at markdown.ts:235-238 (pinned by the test at packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/text-actions.test.ts:82-104), and the caller docs-export-button.tsx:108-115 does no pre-sanitization. The sibling sink does gate: pdf-painter.ts:831-834 filters style.href through isSafeUrl with an explicit comment about `javascript:`/`data:` smuggling, and isSafeUrl is already re-exported at packages/docs/src/index.ts:185. I also ruled out an upstream guard that would make this moot: parseHtmlToBlocks (clipboard.ts:526) assigns `style.href = el.getAttribute('href')` with no scheme check at clipboard.ts:596-601 and is reached from the editor paste path at text-editor.ts:1297, and the JSON clipboard restore at clipboard.ts:148-149 copies href verbatim — so a pasted or imported `javascript:`/`data:` href genuinely lands in the model and flows out into the downloaded .md. Repo-wide grep for isSafeUrl|sanitizeUrl|javascript: shows the only docs-side gates are text-editor.ts:1634/1976, url-detect.ts:18 and pdf-painter.ts:834 — none on the serialize path. No counterexample exists; in-lane as unsafe output handling of attacker-controlled URIs into an exported artifact.

finding.summary: New public mutating method `TextEditor.pasteFormat()` has no `this.readOnly` guard, unlike every sibling programmatic mutator; view-only enforcement now depends entirely on two call sites
finding.evidence: `pasteFormat()` (text-editor.ts:399-407) calls `this.saveSnapshot()` and `this.applyStyleToSelection(...)` — a document write — with no `if (this.readOnly) return;`. The class's other programmatic entry point does exactly that: `insertText()` at :674-677 ("View-only mode: block programmatic text injection"), as do the pointer/keyboard/composition handlers (:677, :730, :932, :1255, :1439). `TextEditor` is a public export of the package (packages/docs/src/index.ts:111) and is embedded by `TextBoxEditor` (view/text-box-editor.ts:48), which never passes `readOnly` at all. Today the only reachable paths are the keydown case (blocked by the read-only early-return at text-editor.ts:932-948) and `EditorAPI.pasteFormat`, which the hand-maintained allowlist neuters (editor.ts:3850), so I could not complete an exploit chain on this branch — but the class-level invariant "a mutating TextEditor method refuses in read-only" is now broken, and any future holder of a read-only TextEditor (e.g. a slides text-box mounted read-only, or a new EditorAPI passthrough) writes to a document the viewer may not own.

verdict.reason: The in-method `this.readOnly` check really is absent from `pasteFormat()` (text-editor.ts:399-407), but every path that can reach it in read-only mode is already guarded, so there is no authorization weakness. Repo-wide grep for `pasteFormat` yields exactly two source call sites: text-editor.ts:1205 (Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+V) — unreachable in read-only because handleKeyDown's read-only branch (text-editor.ts:932-948) returns for every non-navigation key, and 'v' is not navigation — and editor.ts:2906 (EditorAPI), which is explicitly overridden with `api.pasteFormat = () => false` at editor.ts:3847-3850. I also enumerated every `new TextEditor(` construction: editor.ts:2213 (the only one that can be read-only) and text-box-editor.ts:668, which never passes the flag, so the hypothesised read-only slides text box does not exist in this tree. Additionally, client-side `readOnly` is not the enforced authorization boundary: editor.ts:3827-3828 states the server is authoritative, and packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts implements the Yorkie auth webhook with per-document r/rw verbs and share-link/role resolution (lines 14, 59-60, 117-194), so a browser-side guard could never be an access control in any case. What remains is a defense-in-depth/class-invariant consistency concern for hypothetical future callers — a correctness/design matter, not a security defect.
